license_policy: Only CC0 1.0 or Public Domain Mark clips, or clips generated with ffmpeg (breath and sigh only, when no CC0 recording exists). No attribution is legally required, but every source is credited here.
selection: Two clips per tag per gender from Openverse searches '<gender> <tag>' (license=cc0; plus 'man crying' and 'man laughing'), chosen by title, tags and duration. Each item's license was re-checked on the Openverse detail endpoint and on the Freesound landing page (an item whose page did not show CC0 was skipped).
processing: ffmpeg: decode to mono 44.1 kHz, highpass 100 Hz, trim to the loudest window of at most 1.45 s (whole clip if shorter, leading/trailing silence below -45 dBFS removed), gain to -20 dBFS RMS with peaks kept under -1 dBFS (alimiter), 30 ms fades, libmp3lame mono 64 kbps, metadata stripped. Rejected if the source window was quieter than -38 dBFS RMS, the output RMS was below -40 dBFS, its zero-crossing rate was below 150 Hz (rumble), it ran over 1.5 s or exceeded 40 KB.
fields: file, tag, gender, title, creator, license, license_url, source_url, attribution, openverse_id, provider, license_checked, trim (seconds in the source preview), and output measures (rms_db, peak_db, zcr_hz, duration_s, bytes).
gaps_note: No gaps: every tag had CC0 recordings for both genders, so the generated breath/sigh fallback was not needed.

review_T10: T10 re-checked the five clips the controller's ASR pass flagged (female/breath-1, male/sigh-2, male/sob-1, male/sob-2, female/sob-2): whisper base.en and small.en on clips padded with 0.5 s of silence, plus a voicing and rhythm measure (voiced-frame fraction, median f0, peak of the envelope modulation spectrum). Laughter shows as a regular 4-7 Hz voiced pulse; breaths and sighs are mostly unvoiced. One clip was kept with that evidence and four were replaced from the same CC0 Openverse/Freesound candidate pool, with the same processing and license checks. A candidate in which whisper heard words ('R21-33-Man Sobs': 'Dead quiet, please.') was rejected.
